citation: Leone A, De Amicis R, Bertoli S, et al. Absence of a sexual dimorphism in postprandial glucose metabolism after administration of a balanced mixed meal in healthy young volunteers. Nutrition & Diabetes. 2022;12:6.
protocol: Balanced mixed meal after an overnight fast (white-bread sandwich with ham and other items; Table 1 gives grams), sized to 40% of estimated daily energy expenditure, ~60% carbohydrate / 25% fat / 15% protein, ~9 g fibre per 1000 kcal; Table 1 prints energy, carbohydrate, protein and fat grams for women and men separately. Venous samples at 0, 10, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180 min.
population: 36 healthy young volunteers, 18 men and 18 women; age 23.9 ± 2.8 y; BMI 21.9 ± 1.7 kg/m2; Italy (Milan).

reports.where: Table 4: fasting, time to peak, peak and AUC 0-180 by sex; Table 3: mixed-model change from baseline at each time with 95% CI

note: Best single mixed-meal anchor here: meal grams per sex, dense sampling, and insulin peak/AUC in a table. Table 4 seems to give SD while figures and Table 3 use SEM or 95% CI, so check the label on each table. Insulin is in U/l (µU/ml). Only in figures: absolute concentration time courses (Figure). Meal kinds: mixed meal. Uncertainty is SD in Table 4 and SEM or 95% CI elsewhere.
